slides.title: Hot flushes and night sweats: what the NHS suggests
Keep the bedroom cool
slides.body: And wear lightweight clothing to bed.

slides.title: Cool down quickly
slides.body: A cool shower, a fan or a cold drink.

slides.title: Notice your triggers
slides.body: The NHS names spicy food, caffeine, hot drinks, smoking and alcohol. Yours might be different, which is why it helps to write them down.

slides.title: Look after the basics
slides.body: Regular exercise, a healthy weight and ways to bring stress down. CBT can also help with hot flushes.

slides.title: Talk to your GP
slides.body: About how to improve your symptoms and what treatments may suit you.

slides.title: Log the nights, spot the pattern
slides.body: Clari keeps a private record of symptoms and triggers, ready for your GP.
